question: For how long a person can serve as a minister without being a member of either House of Parliament of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6 consecutive months**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Article 75(5) of the Constitution of India**: According to this provision, a person can serve as a minister for a maximum of **6 consecutive months** without being a member of either House of Parliament. During this period, they must get elected as a Member of Parliament to continue serving as a minister.
 
• This rule applies to both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, ensuring that all ministers are accountable to the legislature. *Hence, the correct option is 6 consecutive months.*
 
• After the expiration of the 6-month period, if the individual has not been elected to either House, they must resign from their position as a minister.
